sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这档播客中，我们探讨 20 多岁时会遇到的一些重大生活变动和过渡，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello everybody, welcome back to the show, welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目，欢迎回到这档播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, thanks for tuning in.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，感谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: It's so great to have you back for another episode of The Psychology of Your 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你们能回来收听《The Psychology of Your 20s》的又一期节目。

sentences.en: Today, by popular demand, we're going to be discussing the psychology of a quarter-life crisis.
sentences.zh: 今天，应广大听众的要求，我们将讨论“四分之一人生危机”的心理学。

sentences.en: I'm sure we've all heard of a midlife crisis that typically happens in our late 40s, early 50s.
sentences.zh: 我相信大家都听说过通常发生在 40 多岁末或 50 多岁初的“中年危机”。

sentences.en: You know, the archetype of men buying convertibles and leaving their wives or their partners, women dyeing their hair pink or purple or getting a poodle, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那种典型的刻板印象：男人买敞篷车、抛妻弃子，女人把头发染成粉色或紫色，或者养只贵宾犬，我不知道，

sentences.en: marrying younger people, quitting their jobs, all of those well-known tropes and stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 娶更年轻的人、辞职，所有这些众所周知的桥段和刻板印象。

sentences.en: I feel like this is a pretty highly recognized and satirized concept, but what about the quarter-life crisis that usually happens in our 20s?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个被高度认知和讽刺的概念，但发生在我们 20 多岁时的“四分之一人生危机”又是什么呢？

sentences.en: It doesn't seem like many people are talking about that as much.
sentences.zh: 似乎没多少人像讨论中年危机那样讨论它。

sentences.en: Maybe you're hearing it for the first time today, but I assure you it is very much a real thing.
sentences.zh: 也许你今天是第一次听说，但我向你保证，这绝对是真实存在的。

sentences.en: It's an important thing to discuss.
sentences.zh: 这是一个值得讨论的重要话题。

sentences.en: So the term quarter-life crisis, it's relatively new across the field of psychology and self-help and wellness, but essentially what it explains
sentences.zh: “四分之一人生危机”这个词在心理学、自助和健康领域相对较新，但它本质上解释的是

sentences.en: is a period of panic, of uncertainty, a meltdown of sorts, where we start asking ourselves these really big existential questions we may not have thought about before.
sentences.zh: 一段充满恐慌、不确定性、某种程度上的崩溃时期，我们开始问自己一些以前可能从未想过的重大存在主义问题。

sentences.en: The outcome of that is somewhat of a crisis moment where we feel completely shocked and lost and looking to make some big changes.
sentences.zh: 其结果是一种危机时刻，我们感到极度震惊和迷茫，并寻求做出一些重大改变。

sentences.en: More often than not, it's centered on those three big things, career, love, context, or location.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，它集中在三个大方面：事业、爱情、背景或地点。

sentences.en: I know that sounds like four, but career, love, context, or location is three.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来像四个，但事业、爱情、背景或地点其实是三个。

sentences.en: We begin to feel worried about what we're doing in our lives, whether our relationships fulfill us, whether our lives fulfill us, and if we're in the right place.
sentences.zh: 我们开始担心自己生活中所做的事情，担心人际关系是否让我们满足，生活是否让我们满足，以及我们是否处于正确的位置。

sentences.en: So how can psychology explain this occurrence, this period of intense instability and uncertainty and questioning, this period of intense fear?
sentences.zh: 那么心理学如何解释这种现象，这段充满强烈不稳定、不确定、质疑和恐惧的时期？

sentences.en: How can it explain the subsequent kind of inexplicable urge to change up our lives, to quit our jobs, move to a new city, break up with our long-term partners, shave our heads,
sentences.zh: 它如何解释随之而来那种无法解释的改变生活的冲动，比如辞职、搬到新城市、与长期伴侣分手、剃光头，

sentences.en: completely transform ourselves?
sentences.zh: 彻底改变自己？

sentences.en: This is something I am so interested in, especially as I can feel my own quarter-life crisis kind of looming.
sentences.zh: 我对这一点非常感兴趣，尤其是当我感觉到自己的“四分之一人生危机”隐约逼近时。

sentences.en: In fact, I feel like I'm already very much in it in some ways, and I'm sure many of you are in the same boat as I am and as many of us are,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得自己在某些方面已经深陷其中了，我相信你们很多人也和我一样，和我们许多人一样，

sentences.en: especially as our late 20s and 30s approach and we're surveying our surroundings and freaking out a little bit.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当我们接近 20 多岁末和 30 岁时，我们审视周围的环境，会感到有点恐慌。

sentences.en: So I think it's really important to kind of tackle some of those unanswerable questions in a way, you know, where is my place in the world?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，以某种方式去解决那些无法回答的问题非常重要，你知道，我在这个世界上的位置在哪里？

sentences.en: What is my purpose?
sentences.zh: 我的人生目标是什么？

sentences.en: What the actual heck am I doing with my life?
sentences.zh: 我到底在干什么？

sentences.en: Well, whilst I might not be able to answer those questions for you today, what we will be doing is starting from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 好吧，虽然我今天可能无法为你解答这些问题，但我们将从头开始。

sentences.en: What is a quarter-life crisis?
sentences.zh: 什么是四分之一人生危机？

sentences.en: What does the experience indicate about our growth and our journey?
sentences.zh: 这种经历预示着我们的成长和旅程的什么？

sentences.en: Why do we tend to panic as we enter the tail end of our 20s?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们在 20 多岁末期容易感到恐慌？

sentences.en: And finally, perhaps the most important element of this episode is how do we use this experience as a springboard for our growth and self-actualization and greater happiness.
sentences.zh: 最后，也许本期节目最重要的一点是，我们如何利用这种经历作为我们成长、自我实现和获得更大幸福的跳板。

sentences.en: So, so much amazing content to cover, so much learning to come, I hope.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多精彩的内容要涵盖，希望会有很多收获。

sentences.en: So buckle in for this week's deep dive into the quarter-life crisis.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带，开始本周对“四分之一人生危机”的深度解析吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so we need to start from square one and get our basics down pat.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们需要从零开始，把基础知识搞清楚。

sentences.en: What is a quarter-life crisis?
sentences.zh: 什么是四分之一人生危机？

sentences.en: When we talk about a quarter-life crisis, we're thinking primarily about that period in our lives when we hit our 20s.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论四分之一人生危机时，我们主要指的是 20 多岁的那段时期。

sentences.en: For most of us, it's at this stage that we really start looking at our lives and probably thinking, we have a good 80 or so years on this planet.
sentences.zh: 对于我们大多数人来说，正是在这个阶段，我们开始审视自己的生活，并可能想到：我们在地球上大约有 80 年的时间。

sentences.en: We are a quarter of the way through that, hence the word quarter.
sentences.zh: 我们已经走过了四分之一，所以才叫“四分之一”。

sentences.en: And the reality of the finality of life can really just hit us square on.
sentences.zh: 而生命终结的现实真的会直接冲击我们。

sentences.en: That here we are at 23, 24, 25 years of age, whatever age we're at, and we are a quarter of a way through our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们现在 23、24、25 岁，无论多大，我们已经走过了人生的四分之一。

sentences.en: And what, what do we have to show for that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们有什么成就吗？

sentences.en: What are we even doing?
sentences.zh: 我们到底在做什么？

sentences.en: Firstly, something to get straight.
sentences.zh: 首先，有一点要明确。

sentences.en: This experience is absolutely normal.
sentences.zh: 这种经历是非常正常的。

sentences.en: And I think I would be more concerned if someone didn't have this experience because it's a pivotal moment of redirection, of clarity and growth
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得如果有人没有这种经历，我反而会更担心，因为这是一个关键的重定向、清晰和成长的时刻，

sentences.en: that is essential for our development.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的发展至关重要。

sentences.en: A quarter-life crisis, it's not a clinical term.
sentences.zh: “四分之一人生危机”并不是一个临床术语。

sentences.en: You're not going to find it in the DSM or get a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 你不会在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》(DSM) 中找到它，也不会得到诊断。

sentences.en: It's actually a very subjective, highly individual, kind of existential crisis of sorts that is often seen in people in a certain phase of life who've started asking themselves
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种非常主观、高度个人化、某种程度上的存在主义危机，通常出现在人生某个阶段的人身上，他们开始问自己

sentences.en: some pretty big questions that they've never asked themselves before.
sentences.zh: 一些以前从未问过自己的重大问题。

sentences.en: And this results in some really deep and scary soul-searching around some of those critical components of our life, our careers, our relationships, our financial situation,
sentences.zh: 这导致了对我们生活中一些关键组成部分的深度且可怕的灵魂拷问，比如我们的事业、人际关系、财务状况、

sentences.en: our ambitions.
sentences.zh: 我们的抱负。

sentences.en: Massive, massive things to tackle all at one time.
sentences.zh: 这些都是需要同时处理的巨大、巨大的事情。

sentences.en: And if you're finding yourself in this period of stress, of doubt, of anxiety, kind of wanting to borrow down or run away, you're certainly not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己正处于这种压力、怀疑、焦虑的时期，想要逃避或躲起来，你绝对不是一个人。

sentences.en: I found this LinkedIn study, I think it was done last year or maybe the year before, but it found that 72% of the young people they surveyed had experienced
sentences.zh: 我看到过一项 LinkedIn 的研究，我想是去年或前年做的，它发现 72% 的受访年轻人经历过

sentences.en: some form of a quarter-life crisis with 33% of them currently kind of in the throes of said quarter-life crisis.
sentences.zh: 某种形式的四分之一人生危机，其中 33% 的人目前正处于这种危机之中。

sentences.en: It's such a common experience,
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常普遍的经历，

sentences.en: And the average age of this crisis is about 26 to 27 and it lasts about 11 months, but it can happen at any age, at any time around this period.
sentences.zh: 这种危机的平均年龄大约是 26 到 27 岁，持续约 11 个月，但它可能发生在这个时期的任何年龄、任何时间。

sentences.en: This estimation or figure of, you know,
sentences.zh: 这个估计或数字，你知道，

sentences.en: 26 to 27, though it makes sense, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 26 到 27 岁，虽然有道理，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's at this age that our 30s are looming, the next major chapter of adulthood, we feel like we have enough life experience to be an adult, but don't exactly feel that way.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个年龄，30 岁即将来临，这是成年的下一个主要篇章，我们觉得我们有足够的生活经验成为一个成年人，但并不完全有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Sometimes we find ourselves starting completely from scratch, completely from scratch, you know, ending long-term relationships with people we thought we would marry,
sentences.zh: 有时我们发现自己完全从零开始，真的完全从零开始，你知道，结束了我们以为会结婚的长期关系，

sentences.en: suddenly finding ourselves really dissatisfied with our professional lives, wishing we'd made a different choice, and just feeling all around super loSt.
sentences.zh: 突然发现自己对职业生活非常不满，希望自己当初做了不同的选择，整个人感觉超级迷茫。

sentences.en: And whilst that internal struggle is happening, what's going on around us?
sentences.zh: 当这种内心挣扎发生时，我们周围发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, we're seeing people that we know slowly get married, have children,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们看到认识的人慢慢结婚、生子、

sentences.en: live their passion, get promoted, and, you know, seem like they have everything together, whilst we, at least from personal experience, are still making mistakes,
sentences.zh: 追求自己的热情、获得晋升，而且，你知道，看起来他们一切都处理得很好，而我们，至少从个人经验来看，还在犯错，

sentences.en: and that can really exacerbate already those internal feelings of dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 这真的会加剧内心那种不满的感觉。

sentences.en: I had this experience the other day, actually, whereby most of my friends have these lovely partners, the people they've essentially decided to spend their lives with,
sentences.zh: 前几天我就有这种经历，我大多数朋友都有了可爱的伴侣，那些他们基本上决定共度余生的人，

sentences.en: and I'm still here with my bad date stories, you know, another failed talking stage or terrible but funny hook-up story, making the same mistakes, doing the same thing,
sentences.zh: 而我还在讲着糟糕的约会故事，你知道，又是另一段失败的暧昧期，或者糟糕但好笑的约会故事，犯着同样的错误，做着同样的事情，

sentences.en: that I've done since I was
sentences.zh: 我从

sentences.en: 18 or 19, whilst everyone around me seems to have grown up, you know, seems to have gotten everything together.
sentences.zh: 18 或 19 岁起就一直在做，而周围的每个人似乎都长大了，你知道，似乎一切都步入正轨了。

sentences.en: I think another thing to consider is that our
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一点需要考虑，那就是我们的

sentences.en: 20s are this weird vacuum between our teenage years and what we see as proper adulthood, you know, our 30s and our 40s, and there are all of these opposing kind of decisions
sentences.zh: 20 多岁是青少年时期和我们所认为的真正成年（即 30 多岁和 40 多岁）之间的一个奇怪真空期，你知道，有所有这些相互矛盾的决定

sentences.en: and opposites to consider.
sentences.zh: 和对立面需要考虑。

sentences.en: We have these societal expectations that we should be getting settled, we should settle down, but our brains are still developing and we're still exploring what we would like
sentences.zh: 我们有社会期望，认为我们应该安定下来，应该成家立业，但我们的大脑仍在发育，我们仍在探索自己想要

sentences.en: to be.
sentences.zh: 成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: We feel like we need to have a grasp over things like our finances and our careers, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们需要掌控财务和事业，但与此同时，

sentences.en: we're seeing all of these other things around us change.
sentences.zh: 我们看到周围所有其他事物都在变化。

sentences.en: We're having all of these deep conversations and questions of ourselves and externally in the real world, you know, there's massive inflation, there's unemployment, climate change,
sentences.zh: 我们对自己进行着所有这些深刻的对话和质疑，而在外部现实世界中，你知道，有巨大的通货膨胀、失业、气候变化、

sentences.en: unaffordable housing, lower incomes compared to the expectations that were set by the generation before us, by our parents.
sentences.zh: 住房负担不起、收入低于上一代人（我们的父母）设定的期望。

sentences.en: Those expectations of having it together, of having a house, of knowing what you want to do with your life, they're no longer realistic.
sentences.zh: 那些关于一切步入正轨、拥有房子、知道自己想做什么的期望，已经不再现实了。

sentences.en: I've been having this conversation and this discussion with my friends more and more where our childhood visions of our lives are just no longer realistic, like it's just
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们越来越多地进行这种对话和讨论，我们童年时对生活的憧憬已经不再现实了，就像它

sentences.en: not happening.
sentences.zh: 根本不会发生。

sentences.en: We're not going to be millionaires anytime soon at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少我们短期内不会成为百万富翁。

sentences.en: We start to abandon some of our big aspirations, normally that's creative endeavors like our musical or artistic ambitions.
sentences.zh: 我们开始放弃一些宏大的抱负，通常是那些创造性的追求，比如音乐或艺术梦想。

sentences.en: We forget about, you know, the white picket fence or a home on the beach or being a world traveler because that now costs like millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了，你知道，白色栅栏的房子、海边的家或者环游世界，因为那现在需要花费数百万美元。

sentences.en: It costs a lot of money and that realization that what we wanted as children isn't exactly as achievable
sentences.zh: 这需要很多钱，而意识到我们童年时想要的东西并不像看起来那么容易实现，

sentences.en: as it seemed is such a bitter, hard pill to swallow and it can be a massive trigger for what will become a quarter life crisis.
sentences.zh: 这真是一颗苦涩、难以下咽的药丸，它可能成为引发四分之一人生危机的巨大导火索。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes where we are right now isn't where we want to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时我们现在所处的位置并不是我们想要的位置。

sentences.en: It's not where we imagined we would be at this age.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们想象中在这个年龄应该达到的位置。

sentences.en: You thought things would turn out differently and they're not.
sentences.zh: 你以为事情会变得不同，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You know, when I was
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我

sentences.en: 16, I thought I was going to be really successful by now, like really successful, you know, maybe even married or at least with someone I love.
sentences.zh: 16 岁时，我以为我现在会非常成功，真的很成功，你知道，甚至可能结婚了，或者至少和我爱的人在一起。

sentences.en: I thought
sentences.zh: 我以为

sentences.en: I'd be a homeowner.
sentences.zh: 我会拥有自己的房子。

sentences.zh: 有一个陈词滥调，我认为我们在谈论这个话题时经常被重复，我讨厌陈词滥调，但我还是要在这里重复一遍。

sentences.en: Hitting rock bottom is such a great spring board up.
sentences.zh: 跌入谷底是绝佳的触底反弹跳板。

sentences.en: I know, I know, it's so cliche, but like the saying always goes, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道，这太老套了，但就像那句老话说的，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, the only way is up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，唯一的出路就是向上。

sentences.en: If we never hit rock bottom, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们从未跌入谷底，对吧？

sentences.en: We never get pushed to the point of questioning our lives because we remain where it's, you know, just comfortable enough to feel safe and secure, but not happy.
sentences.zh: 我们就永远不会被推到质疑生活的地步，因为我们一直待在那个“足够舒适”的地方，感到安全和稳定，但并不快乐。

sentences.en: And when we hit a crisis point where we have to reevaluate everything because it's falling apart, you're kind of forced into a place of reflection and you gain a new perspective
sentences.zh: 而当我们到达危机点，不得不重新评估一切，因为一切都在分崩离析时，你会被迫进入一个反思的空间，你获得了新的视角，

sentences.en: and you're given this like magical, magical opportunity of a fresh start, you gain humility, you see that life is not black and white and you begin to let go of the things that
sentences.zh: 你被赋予了这种神奇的、神奇的重新开始的机会，你获得了谦逊，你看到生活不是非黑即白的，你开始放下那些

sentences.en: you can't control.
sentences.zh: 你无法控制的事情。

sentences.en: Because when you're in like a crisis, when you're in like fight or flight mode, like those unimportant things like how people perceive you or what you're wearing or whether
sentences.zh: 因为当你处于危机中，当你处于“战斗或逃跑”模式时，那些不重要的事情，比如别人怎么看你，或者你穿什么，或者

sentences.en: people think I'm smart enough or whether I'm doing the right internships or getting the right jobs and all these things like they really don't matter because you're in crisis
sentences.zh: 别人是否觉得我足够聪明，或者我是否在做正确的实习，或者在做正确的工作，所有这些事情，它们真的不重要，因为你处于危机

sentences.en: mode, you're in a meltdown.

sentences.en: The only things that matter to you are the things that are really important and in that way you get to identify them clearer.
sentences.zh: 唯一对你重要的事情，就是那些真正重要的事情，通过这种方式，你可以更清晰地识别它们。

sentences.en: Finally, I think a quarter-life crisis strengthens your core values.

sentences.en: I know I talk a lot about values on the show because I think they are really important to establish in our
sentences.zh: 我知道我在节目中经常谈论价值观，因为我认为在我们的

sentences.en: 20s and to take some time to think about like what are the five things that are most important to you?

sentences.en: Is it humility?

sentences.en: And often we go through life, especially early adulthood, really following the values that were instilled to us by our parents and by our families and our communities.
sentences.zh: 我们往往在生活中，特别是在成年早期，真正遵循的是父母、家庭和社区灌输给我们的价值观。

sentences.en: These values are really easy to partake in because they don't require any effort and they've all we've ever known.
sentences.zh: 这些价值观很容易遵循，因为它们不需要任何努力，而且是我们所知的一切。

sentences.en: but often a trigger for a quarter-life crisis is that these values no longer fit and they no longer fit how we perceive the world.
sentences.zh: 但“四分之一人生危机”的导火索往往是这些价值观不再适用，不再符合我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: So we're forced to either abandon them and create new ones or strengthen elements of them that we do believe in.
sentences.zh: 所以我们被迫要么放弃它们并创造新的价值观，要么加强我们真正相信的那些部分。

sentences.en: I think religion is a good example here.

sentences.zh: 你知道，我想说我们很多人是在某种宗教社会中长大的，或者有着某种宗教背景或宗教知识，这通常围绕着一个

sentences.zh: 上帝或某种关于善恶的传统信仰。

sentences.en: And those values are often instilled in us by our parents who are raising us the best they can, giving us the knowledge that their parents gave them.
sentences.zh: 这些价值观通常是由父母灌输给我们的，他们尽其所能抚养我们，把他们父母传给他们的知识传给我们。

sentences.en: But you actually really need to consider whether you believe in those things and whether you believe in the values that were instilled to you as a child.
sentences.zh: 但你实际上真的需要考虑你是否相信这些事情，以及你是否相信儿时灌输给你的价值观。

sentences.en: You know, using that religion example, you might no longer believe in God if you test that feeling and you test that relationship and you test that belief.

sentences.en: But what you find you do believe in is something bigger or that, you know, love is at the core of everything.
sentences.zh: 但你发现你确实相信某种更宏大的东西，或者，你知道，爱是万物的核心。

sentences.en: And that brings us comfort because we know we believe in that.
sentences.zh: 这给我们带来了安慰，因为我们知道我们相信这一点。

sentences.en: It's not just something that our parents have told us.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是父母告诉我们的东西。

sentences.zh: 我们知道我们可以信任这种信念，因为它是我们为自己创造的。

sentences.zh: 所以，如果这一集有一个要点，那就是这种经历，这种我们在20多岁时很多人发现自己正在经历的生命危机，以及我们的
